_source: Actor spans for post_composer's acting-party check. 'replay': every distinct actor span the Action Center's claim calls returned, 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-15 (264 calls recorded in production llm_generation_samples, task action_center_claim), as compose() reads it (_source_spelling), labelled by hand. 'variation': phrases written for this set on 2026-10-15 to cover the shapes the replay sample shows too few of: actors with no capitalised word (role descriptions, groups of officials, agencies by common noun), named parties with invented names, and non-actors of every kind the composer must refuse (actions and decisions, documents, money and counts, events, laws, places and times, bare pronouns), and headline fragments that carry a verb after an acting subject. Rerun scripts/calibrate_claim_actor.py after any change (a test fails until you do).
_rubric: actor = the span's leading noun phrase names or describes a party that can act or speak: a person (by name or by role: 'a federal judge', 'the president', 'the senator's lawyer'), an institution, company or organisation, an official body, a government (including one named by its country or capital), or a group of such people ('federal agents', 'a bipartisan group of senators', 'voters'). The LEADING noun phrase, because compose() renders the span as the claim's subject: a headline fragment the model returns with its verb ('U.S. imposes sweeping sanctions') still makes its subject the claim's. Not an actor = anything else: an action, decision or event ('the settlement', 'the move', 'the vote'), a document, report, poll or data, a law, policy or program, an amount or count of things, a market or price, a place or time used as one ('in the Senate', 'last week'), a bare pronoun, or a party named only through a pronoun ('his lawyers', 'its board'): either way the rendered claim could not say who.
